newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa confident PGM supply to return to normal.
newsitem.headline: Degussa confident PGM supply to return to normal.

text.p: German catalytic converter maker Degussa AG said on Tuesday it was confident Russian platinum group metals (PGM) sales to the western world were being resumed and supply flows should return to normal in second half 1997.
"Russia is back in the spot market offering material so the situation has become more comfortable there," said the company's head of precious metals trading, Ralf Drieselmann.
"But lease rates are still exceptionally high."
Russian precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport earlier confirmed reports that it had resumed long-delayed PGM deliveries to the main consumer, Japan, last week.
Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium and 20 percent of its platinum.
Ending a six-month hiatus, the Russian move was welcomed by Degussa, which accounts for 15 to 25 percent of world catalytic converter production, the main area of PGM consumption.
Drieselmann said there were no PGM supply shortages at Degussa and there had not been any -- although this had not been ruled out in early June.
He expected downward pressure on PGM prices from a more relaxed supply scenario, but added lease rates had yet to reflect Russia's re-emergence.
The one-month lease rate for palladium was at 65 percent and platinum at 38 percent on Tuesday, compared with the average of many years for both metals of between two and five percent.
"I suspect that either supplies are still very tight or lenders are seeking to exploit the earlier tightness," he said.
But the rates were down from around 200 percent in June, when the supply crisis was most acute.
The crisis had encouraged the automobile industry to start exploring palladium substitutes in order to lessen its dependence on Russia, Drieselmann said.
The electronics industry was already successfully experimenting with alternative metals such as nickel and copper.
